injuries.summary:
### NFL injury briefing: key updates

- **Cardinals LT Paris Johnson Jr.** — out for the season after tearing his **left biceps**. He’s set for surgery soon.  
  **Why it matters:** Arizona loses its starting left tackle, a major hit to pass protection and run blocking.  
  **Watch next:** who replaces him at LT.

- **Eagles RB Saquon Barkley** — **week-to-week** with a **hamstring** injury and is **unlikely to play Sunday vs. the Jaguars in London**.  
  **Why it matters:** Philly’s offense loses its top back, with clear fantasy fallout.  
  **Watch next:** Barkley’s practice status and whether the Eagles adjust the backfield rotation.

- **Eagles OL Cam Jurgens** — entered **concussion protocol** after self-reporting symptoms Monday. He played all 61 snaps vs. the Rams.  
  **Why it matters:** Philadelphia’s offensive line is thinner, and the Friday flight to London could make clearance harder.  
  **Watch next:** whether Jurgens clears in time; **Willie Lampkin** would likely step in if he can’t go.

- **Vikings LG Donovan Jackson** — likely **season-ending surgery** for a **meniscus tear**.  
  **Why it matters:** Minnesota loses another interior OL starter, adding more strain up front.  
  **Watch next:** the official surgery timeline and replacement plan.

- **Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw** — in the **concussion protocol**.  
  **Why it matters:** The Vikings may be down both starting left-side blockers.  
  **Watch next:** his practice participation and clearance progress.

- **Bears RB Kyle Monangai** — **day-to-day**.  
  **Why it matters:** This looks short-term, but it’s worth monitoring after a big workload game.  
  **Watch next:** whether he practices and how Chicago handles backfield touches.

- **Rams WR Konata Mumpfield** and **Forbes** — both suffered **minor injuries**.  
  **Why it matters:** No major alarm yet.  
  **Watch next:** whether either misses practice time.

### Returning from injury
- **No clear returns from injury were specified in today’s updates.**

- **Brian Robinson (RB)** — He logged 14 carries and scored three times in the Saints win, while Bijan Robinson still dominated the team’s overall rushing output with 19 carries for 145 yards and two TDs. That points to a real two-RB setup: Bijan stays the top-volume/floor play, but Brian has enough short-yardage and goal-line work to matter for TD-driven fantasy projections this week. [2,5,12]

- **Kyle Pitts (TE)** — He did not start and had only one snap in two series, with Charlie Woerner, Nick Muse and Austin Hooper all seeing more work while the team said Pitts is healthy. For Week 5, Pitts’ route and target share look less secure than a normal TE starter, and the other tight ends are the direct beneficiaries if this usage holds. [4]

- **Michael Penix Jr. (QB)** — Atlanta has averaged 40.0 points with Penix and only 8.0 without him, and the Falcons have piled up 80 points over the last two games since he returned. That keeps the entire ATL offense upgraded for fantasy/DFS, and it makes the passing game and scoring environment more trustworthy even if this matchup tilts run-heavy against a Baltimore front that is already depleted up front in the game context. [1,2,10]

- **Jake Matthews (LT)** — His groin injury pushed Michael Jerrell into the lineup, and Jerrell was on the field for Brian Robinson’s scoring run. If Matthews sits again, Atlanta’s protection and run-blocking efficiency take a hit, which matters more for Penix’s efficiency and Bijan/Brian’s per-carry outlook than for their volume. [6]

- **Lamar Jackson (QB), Ravens** — Baltimore is uncertain whether Jackson will play Sunday night. If he’s out or limited, Atlanta’s defense gets a cleaner sack/turnover projection; if he suits up, the Falcons DST gets downgraded a bit. [11]
